subject: platform/distribution
professional: a release engineer / package-registry maintainer who ships npm, PyPI and Homebrew packages and store extensions (the person who would run `npm pack`, build the wheel, `brew audit` the formula and load the unpacked extension before trusting a publisher script with a token)

evidence.correctness: Ran four generators and checked outputs against the target registries' own tooling, not the author's tests. (1) npm: `node npm.mjs --pack slopsquatting-check` then `npm pack --dry-run` accepted it (6 files, valid name/version/bin/files/engines/license/repository.directory, package.json fields match the npm docs); the generated bin.mjs run through a symlink printed the CLI usage (the symlink-argv[1] wrapper the README describes works). (2) PyPI: `pypi.mjs --pack flaky-test-finder`, `tomllib` parsed the pyproject (PEP 621 fields valid), `python -m build --wheel` in a venv built flaky_test_finder-0.1.2, METADATA is Metadata-Version 2.4 with Requires-Python, Project-URLs, license file and console_scripts entry; pip-installed and `flaky-test-finder --help` ran. (3) WebExtension: `webext.mjs --build 1099k-reconciliation-worksheet`, manifest is valid MV3 (manifest_version 3, action, service_worker, icons 16/48/128, no permissions), `unzip -t` on the hand-rolled zip passed (all entries OK), the inline script was moved to inline-1.js so no inline code remains except ld+json data, name <=45 and description <=132 as Chrome requires. (4) Homebrew: called formula() directly; class name, url (including scoped `@s/x/-/x-0.1.0.tgz` form), sha256 and install block match the Homebrew node-formula pattern (`std_npm_args`, `install_symlink Dir["#{libexec}/bin/*"]`), `#{` is escaped. I did not have `brew` here, so the formula was not run through `brew audit`. One real output defect found: desc is escaped and then sliced to 80, which can cut between a backslash and its quote and leave an unterminated Ruby string (reproduced with a quote-heavy description; only latent for today's descriptions). Dry runs of npm.mjs/pypi.mjs/webext.mjs ran and list sensible plans (npm 5 of 7 qualify, 2 skipped because the name belongs to another project; webext 1227 of 1316).
evidence.completeness: README (portfolio/distribution/README.md) and file headers claim generators for npm, PyPI (single-file and src-layout), Homebrew, VS Code/VSIX, WebExtension, Android TWA, iOS, WordPress, GHCR, Nix flake, pre-commit, GitHub Action, MCP, desktop, social/blog hubs. All 28 modules exist with tests and 14 distribute-*.yml workflows. Checked end to end here: npm, pypi, webext, homebrew formula, dry-run planning, allow-list gating. Not run end to end: live publish paths (need owner tokens, correctly), brew install, VS Code vsce install, store review. Android/iOS emit build inputs and BUILD.md and say explicitly that signing/upload is the account holder's step, which matches what they do.
evidence.verification: Ran each test file separately (a single `node --test '*.test.mjs'` also works but is slow): 27 of 28 files green, 0 failures, e.g. npm 16, pypi 11, homebrew 8, webext 9, hub 23. ios.test.mjs passed its first 7 tests then its 8th (`plan has no duplicate bundle ids across the real catalogue`, builds all ~1300 ventures with icon rendering) exceeded 240 s twice and was killed (exit 124); the whole-suite run sat on it for 6+ minutes. Seeded three mutations: (a) npm.mjs `fresh.length >= MAX_PER_RUN` to `>`: test 14 failed (caught); (b) npm.mjs `!isOurs(doc)` inverted: test 13 failed (caught); (c) homebrew.mjs desc `.slice(0, 80)` to `.slice(0, 90)`: all 8 tests still passed (NOT caught, Homebrew's 80-char limit and the escape-then-slice interaction are untested). All reverted with git checkout; git status shows no change to platform/distribution. Tests mock fetch and the publish function, so the publish gating (live needs both DISTRIBUTE_* and token, MAX_PER_RUN, name-ownership check) is genuinely exercised.
evidence.craft: Read npm.mjs, pypi.mjs, homebrew.mjs, webext.mjs, vscode.mjs (first 120 lines) and the npm/pypi workflows. Good: pure functions (buildPackage/formula/manifest) separate from run(); injectable fetch/publish/log; stateless de-duplication against the registry; ownership check via repository URL; `--provenance`; skip-not-guess when a CLI imports a package; deterministic zip with fixed timestamp. Defects: escape-then-slice in homebrew.mjs rubyString/desc; pypi.mjs STDLIB_OK lists `tomllib` (3.11+) while generated pyproject says `requires-python >=3.9`, so a tool importing it would install on 3.9/3.10 and crash; STDLIB_OK allows `os`/`shutil`, so the comment 'no process spawning' is not enforced (os.system passes); npm.mjs IMPORT_RE is regex-based and misses `require()`/`createRequire` and import in template strings; the Homebrew `test do` only asserts the symlink exists (brew-core would reject; fine for a tap); BASE_URL is the retired github.io address.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'off by default / dry run unless DISTRIBUTE_* var and token' is true in code (npm.mjs:170, pypi.mjs:~156, homebrew.mjs:~51) and in distribute-npm.yml / distribute-pypi.yml / distribute-homebrew.yml (publish step gated on vars.DISTRIBUTE_*; no secrets used by default); desktop workflow is workflow_dispatch only and gated. 'Package asks for no permissions and bundles no remote code' (webext) is true for the build I inspected (no permissions key; cross-origin and network scripts are skipped). 'Qualifying counts' in webext dry run agree with its code. Nothing here publishes under the owner's accounts without the owner setting a repo variable and a secret; the scheduled npm (weekly) and PyPI workflows will publish unattended up to 5 packages per run once the owner sets those, which is the owner's explicit gate, not a bypass. Gaps: the package/formula/extension homepage URLs embed https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/..., which CLAUDE.md says is now only a redirect to https://marisstella.app/; the README text says 'Maris Stella Labs' while linking the old host.
evidence.fitness: The intended user (the owner or an agent wanting registry presence) can run `versions.mjs --write`, dry-run, then flip a variable and token to publish; the produced npm tarball and PyPI wheel installed and ran from a symlinked bin and a venv console script. WebExtension zip loads as MV3 structure and is store-shaped but upload remains manual by design. Limits: no live publish was executed (correctly), so registry acceptance (e.g. npm provenance needs `id-token: write` in the workflow) is not demonstrated; the Homebrew path depends on the npm publish having happened first.
evidence.domain: Compared against npm package.json docs and `npm pack`, PEP 621/PEP 517 and a real wheel build, Chrome MV3 manifest and Web Store limits (45-char name, 132-char description), the Homebrew Node formula cookbook (`std_npm_args`, class naming, desc rules), and VSIX/vsce manifest layout. A registry maintainer would sign off on: scoped-name handling, ownership check before republishing, provenance, version-already-published skip, max-per-run cap. They would object to: regex import scanning instead of an AST, `license = { text }` (deprecated by PEP 639 in favour of SPDX `license =`), unpinned `setuptools>=61`, no sdist+wheel smoke-install in CI before upload, and the weak Homebrew test block.

defects.what: Generated npm/PyPI/Homebrew/WebExt/VS Code metadata link to the retired github.io host (BASE_URL), which CLAUDE.md says is now only a redirect to marisstella.app; every published package would carry a stale homepage that cannot be edited after publish on npm/PyPI without a new version.
pypi.mjs STDLIB_OK includes tomllib (Python 3.11+) but generated pyproject.toml declares requires-python >=3.9, so a qualifying tool using tomllib would install on 3.9/3.10 and fail at import.

homebrew desc is escaped and then sliced to 80 chars; the cut can fall between a backslash and its quote and emit an unterminated Ruby string. Also, shortening the limit (80 to 90) is not caught by any test.
ios.test.mjs's 'plan has no duplicate bundle ids across the real catalogue' builds the whole catalogue and takes over 4 minutes; the aggregate `node --test '*.test.mjs'` effectively stalls on it.
The 'no network, no process spawning' import allowlist admits os and shutil, so os.system/os.popen are not blocked; npm/webext import scanning is regex-based and misses require()/createRequire.
Homebrew test block only asserts the bin symlink exists, a weak smoke test (brew audit --strict / brew-core would ask for running the tool).

verdict: A competent, well-gated publishing toolkit: the npm tarball, PyPI wheel (built, installed, run) and MV3 extension zip I generated were accepted by the registries' own tooling, nothing publishes without the owner setting both a repo variable and a secret, and 27 of 28 test files pass with mutations to the publish-cap and ownership logic caught. It falls short of a 4 because homepage URLs still point at the retired github.io host, the PyPI generator can emit a package that crashes on Python 3.9/3.10 via tomllib, the Homebrew desc truncation can emit invalid Ruby (and an 80-to-90 mutation survived), the Homebrew formula was not run through brew audit, no live publish was exercised, and one test (ios catalogue plan) takes over four minutes. Meets the bar on the computed rule, narrowly.
